_about: Pattern readings where the two runs differ after normalising (group 1 = none for single flashes; a colour cycle read from a different start is the same cycle; a sectored light's main colour is the one named first in its character line). Decided on the source text, 28 Oct 2026.

77.why: The second revolving light is shown only during fogs (Findlay 1887: 'During fogs a smaller bright revolving light ... is shown'); not part of the light as normally seen. Noted on the light.

95.why: 'One bright or red light' with no kind word: Findlay 1879 leaves 'fixed' unsaid for such lights; fixed, kind assumed.

124.why: As 95: two lights, fixed, kind assumed; main colour by the rule (bright named first).

186.why: Dubh Artach: 'fixed or occulting' -- fixed over most of the horizon, occulting (visible 10 and 30 secs. alternately at intervals of 10 secs.) only towards Iona and the Torranan Rocks. Drawn fixed; the occulting sector is noted.

204.why: Revolving 1 min., bright and red alternately: the colour cycle repeats every 120 s.

231.why: 'A group of 4 flashes ... in every min., occupying about 22 secs.': the dark of 38 s follows by arithmetic.

187.why: Rubha nan Gall, 'One fixed light' with no colour in the character line: bright towards Mull Sound (the channel it marks), red to seaward northward, green towards the rocks. Main colour white; red and green are sectors.
